Subject: Bulk inference / async job SLA — request for exception

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited about Redwood's throughput and the KV-cache benefits. Before we finalize procurement, our compliance and SRE teams have a hard requirement around bulk/async job completion windows and retry behavior for scheduled inference. High level asks:

- Job completion window: for large nightly bulk jobs we need an SLA that guarantees completion within 24 hours for jobs up to ~50M tokens.
- Retry semantics: retries must be supported/clear (client retries + server-side best-effort) and we need idempotency guarantees so retried submissions don't double-charge or double-execute.
- Observable status: api/job-status events (webhook or poll) and a retention window for job logs (90 days).

These items are currently blockers for our legal/procurement team. I've attached our current SOW (DataCloud_SOW_v3.pdf) and marked the appendix we'd like to amend. Can Redwood provide a written exception and suggested contract language?

Emma

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear summary and the SOW. Looping Markus (SRE/infra) and Stephanie (sales ops) so we can align contract language and technical constraints.

Short answer: we can support a one-off SLA amendment for long-running batch jobs, but there are a few technical caveats and operational prerequisites we need to include in the contract. High-level points from our side:

- Typical hosted async guarantee: job completion SLO is 4 hours for standard jobs (default capacity). For very large jobs (~>5M tokens) we recommend Redwood Dedicated or reserved slot capacity to meet predictable completion windows.
- Exception path: we can offer a 24-hour completion window for jobs up to 50M tokens as a contractual appendix if DataCloud commits to a reserved capacity plan (monthly commit) or a scheduled nightly maintenance window (we'll need a predictable start window).
- Retries & idempotency: clients must attach a stable job_id/idempotency_key on submission (we surface both in the API). Redwood will ensure server-side deduplication for repeated job_ids for 7 days; beyond that the guarantee expires.
- Observability: job status webhook + poll endpoints available; 90-day log retention can be offered as an add-on.

I've attached a short summary (redwood-async-sla-summary.pdf) that outlines recommended language. If you can confirm the expected job sizes and cadence (daily batch vs ad-hoc), we can draft Appendix B (SLA amendment) for legal review.

Thanks,

Emma / Jasmine — quick technical note from infra: we can meet the proposal with the following constraints and telemetry commitments.

- Idempotency & retries:
  - Job submissions must include an idempotency_key/job_id (UUID recommended). Redwood will perform server-side dedupe for any repeated job_id for 7 days. Dedupe is best-effort for >7 days.
  - Client-side retry guidance: exponential backoff starting at 2s, cap at 120s; include job_id on every retry. We do not recommend blind synchronous retries for large payloads — prefer a submit->job_id->poll or webhook model.

- Job completion windows:
  - For reserved capacity: MTT (mean time to completion) for jobs up to 20M tokens is typically <1 hour; for 20–50M typical MTT is 2–6 hours depending on concurrency and sequence lengths. 24-hour window is achievable if capacity is reserved and job submission is within the agreed window.

- Observability & logging:
  - We will provide job-level events (queued, started, progress pings, completed, failed) as webhooks. Events are retained for 90 days in the customer console.
  - Any server-side automatic retry attempts (for transient infra errors) are logged and surfaced on the job status "events" list.

- Metrics & credits:
  - Suggest metric: monthly % of jobs in the nightly window that complete within 24 hours. Threshold for credit: <99.5% completion triggers credits.
  - Proposed credit formula in draft: 5% credit on monthly invoice if the monthly completion rate falls below 99.5% but above 97.0%; 15% credit if below 97.0%. Credit only applies to the portion of invoice tied to reserved capacity for the nightly window, not to general usage.

I'll attach our implementation notes (batch-idempotency-guidelines.md) and a short table of expected MTTs by job size. Happy to sync on a brief tech call if you want to walk through load profiles.

-Markus

Emma — thanks for the details and the quick internal review. Based on the profile and Markus' notes, Redwood can proceed with a conditional exception and proposed contractual language. Key bullets for Appendix B (draft to be provided to legal):

- Scope: applies to jobs submitted to the async/bulk endpoint during the agreed nightly window (02:00-04:00 PT) with an idempotency_key and total job size <= 50M tokens.
- Commitments: Redwood will "use commercially reasonable efforts" to achieve job completion within 24 hours. For predictability, DataCloud will subscribe to a Reserved Capacity plan (monthly commit).
- Observability: Job-level webhook and poll endpoints; event retention = 90 days. Server-side retries for transient infra failures will be logged on the job events stream.
- Idempotency: server-side dedupe for repeated job_id for 7 days. Client required to supply job_id for retry safety.
- SLA credits (draft): if monthly completion rate within the nightly window <99.5% but >=97.0% then 5% credit on the reserved-capacity portion of the invoice; if <97.0% then 15% credit. Credits apply after two separate incidents in a calendar month.
- Exclusions: force majeure, scheduled maintenance (with notice), customer-caused delays (invalid payloads, missing idempotency key), and torrent-style replays.

Next steps: we will (1) draft Appendix B with the exact wording + credit formula, (2) provide a cost delta and lead time for Dedicated/reserved capacity options, and (3) schedule a short tech sync (30 min) to review telemetry and idempotency implementation.

I'm attaching a proposed amendment document (proposed-sla-amendment.docx) with the initial language — this is a working draft for legal. If that sounds right, I can loop in contracts and get a formal redline.

Thanks,
